content.value_statement: Complex software projects often fail because boundaries, domain rules, and tradeoffs are unclear. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through discovery, modeling, ADRs, and TypeScript architecture scaffolds.
actual_capabilities: Guides architecture discovery with structured questions about actors, constraints, failures, and success measures.
Helps identify domain entities, value objects, aggregates, services, and ubiquitous language.
Maps inbound and outbound ports, adapters, and layer responsibilities for hexagonal systems.
Drafts Architecture Decision Records with context, options, decision drivers, consequences, and risks.
Produces TypeScript-oriented scaffolding patterns for entities, use cases, repositories, controllers, and adapters.
Highlights common Clean Architecture mistakes and shows safer boundary patterns.
limitations: It does not make architecture decisions without user input.
Generated scaffolds are templates and need project-specific validation before production use.
It does not include runnable build scripts or automated code generation commands.
Current best practices may require separate research when frameworks or cloud services have changed.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Service
use_cases.description: Define the core domain, actors, use cases, boundaries, and first ADR before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Refactor a Monolith Module
use_cases.description: Separate domain logic from controllers, persistence, and external services using ports and adapters.

use_cases.title: Standardize Architecture Reviews
use_cases.description: Use repeatable prompts, diagrams, and ADR templates to review tradeoffs across teams.

prompt_templates.title: Start Discovery
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: start a new architecture session.
prompt_templates.prompt: I need to architect a new order management service. Guide me through discovery and ask the first questions.

prompt_templates.title: Model the Domain
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: turn requirements into domain concepts.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me model the domain for a marketplace checkout system. Identify entities, value objects, aggregates, and open questions.

prompt_templates.title: Define Ports and Adapters
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: design service boundaries after domain modeling.
prompt_templates.prompt: Using these domain decisions, define inbound ports, outbound ports, adapters, and layer responsibilities for a hexagonal TypeScript service.

prompt_templates.title: Create ADR and Scaffold
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: document a decision and draft implementation structure.
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft an ADR for choosing Hexagonal Architecture, then outline the TypeScript scaffold for entities, use cases, repositories, and controllers.

output_examples.input: I need to design a subscription billing service.
output: A discovery checklist covering actors, failure modes, compliance constraints, and success criteria.
A draft domain model with subscription, invoice, payment, plan, and account concepts.
A list of unresolved architecture questions to answer before scaffolding.

output_examples.input: We chose ports and adapters for our order service.
output: A boundary map separating domain, application, infrastructure, and interface layers.
Inbound ports for order placement and cancellation.
Outbound ports for persistence, payments, inventory, notifications, and event publishing.

output_examples.input: Document why we are using Hexagonal Architecture.
output: An ADR with context, decision drivers, considered options, chosen decision, consequences, and risks.
Implementation notes for composition root, adapters, and test doubles.

best_practices: Start with discovery before generating scaffolds, unless the architecture decisions already exist.
Record tradeoffs in ADRs while decisions are fresh and still easy to challenge.
Keep domain behavior independent from frameworks, databases, and external services.
anti_patterns: Do not ask it to produce production code before domain rules and boundaries are clear.
Do not treat generated templates as complete implementations without tests and validation.
Do not use architecture patterns where a simpler module structure would meet the real constraints.

faq.question: What architecture style does this skill focus on?
faq.answer: It focuses on Clean Architecture, Hexagonal Architecture, ports and adapters, and domain-driven modeling patterns.

faq.question: Can it generate TypeScript code?
faq.answer: It can draft TypeScript scaffolds and templates, but the output still needs project-specific implementation and tests.

faq.question: Does it choose the architecture for me?
faq.answer: No. It asks questions, presents tradeoffs, and documents decisions that the user makes.

faq.question: Can it help with existing systems?
faq.answer: Yes. It can analyze boundaries, identify coupling, and suggest refactoring steps around ports, adapters, and domain logic.

faq.question: Does it require a specific framework?
faq.answer: No. The examples are TypeScript-oriented, but the architecture guidance is framework independent.

faq.question: Is this a security or compliance review tool?
faq.answer: No. It can surface architecture risks, but it does not replace security, privacy, or compliance review.
